payload.say: Every animal has to find food. A goat eats grass, a tiger eats the goat. But a plant never goes anywhere. So where does a plant get its food from? It makes its own.

payload.say: A leaf needs three things. Sunlight from above, water pulled up from the roots, and a gas from the air called carbon dioxide. Put those three together and the leaf can build food.

payload.say: Inside every leaf there is a green colour called chlorophyll. That green is what catches the sunlight. No chlorophyll, no catching sunlight, no food. That is why almost every leaf you have ever seen is green.

payload.say: The leaf keeps the food it makes, and it lets out oxygen. That is the gas we breathe. So the tree outside your classroom is quietly making the air you are breathing right now.

payload.say: This whole process has a name. Photosynthesis. Photo means light, and synthesis means putting together. Putting food together using light.

Can you tell like what is leaves and how they are creamy color and why they are sometimes in brown color

Leaves are parts of a plant that help it make food. They are usually green because of a pigment called chlorophyll, but some young leaves or leaves with other pigments can look creamy or yellow. When a leaf dries or the plant stops making chlorophyll, the green fades and the leaf turns brown, like when mango leaves fall in the autumn.
